situation: Guidance written for new incident commanders.

moves.name: ask what changed before digging
moves.step: Pull up the change log before opening diagnostic tools.
moves.evidence: The first question is not "what is broken" but "what changed".

moves.name: stabilise now, diagnose tomorrow
moves.step: Mitigate first; schedule diagnosis for when customers are no longer hurting.
moves.evidence: Diagnosis can happen tomorrow; the customer's failed label run cannot be un-failed.

moves.name: match process size to harm and reversibility
moves.step: Choose ticket, short review or full process from blast radius and reversibility.
moves.cue: deciding how much incident machinery to use
moves.evidence: I size the response on two things: how many people are being hurt right now (blast radius), and whether what is happening can be undone

moves.name: give next update time instead of ETA
moves.step: Promise the time of the next update and keep it even if nothing changed.
moves.evidence: Give a time for the next update instead, and keep it even if the update is "no change".

moves.name: price the risk and offer a lower-cost path
moves.step: State who carries the cost of a risky date and offer a way to keep it more cheaply.
moves.cue: a request to ship on a risky date
moves.evidence: Put a price on it: who carries the cost if it goes wrong, and when.

considerations.evidence: anything a customer cannot redo, gets the full process
